programme.title: Ibsen
programme.desc: The 1988 adaption of the classic by Henrik Ibsen. Oppressed by past tragedies and an unhappy marriage, a master builder is haunted by fears that the next generation will knock him off his pedestal.

programme.title: The Australian Wars
programme.desc: The story of Australia's first wars, calling for the nation to acknowledge the First Peoples who died in these conflicts and for the Australian War Memorial to recognise them.

programme.title: Eurovision Classical Concerts
programme.sub-title: Cologne: WDR Symphony Orchestra plays Stravinsky's Petrushka
programme.desc: Celebrating great music-making across Europe, a special concert from the Philharmonic Hall in Cologne, also featuring music by Lyadov, Stravinsky's teacher.

programme.title: British History's Biggest Fibs with Lucy Worsley
programme.desc: Lucy debunks the foundation myth of one of our favourite royal dynasties, the Tudors. According to the history books, after 30 years of bloody battles between the white-rosed Yorkists and the red-rosed Lancastrians, Henry Tudor rid us of civil war and the evil Richard III. But Lucy reveals how the Tudors invented the story of the 'Wars of the Roses' after they came to power to justify their rule.

programme.title: Wild China
programme.desc: China's heartland is the centre of a 5,000-year-old civilisation and is home to the giant panda, the golden snub-nosed monkey and the golden takin. China faces environmental problems, but the relationship the Chinese have with their environment is deep and extraordinary. We will understand what this means for the future of China.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Panel game of word definitions and deceptions, hosted by Robert Robinson. Team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by Patrick Mower, Russell Harty, Nanette Newman and Gabrielle Drake.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Polly Elwes, Richard Baker and John Julius Norwich. With guest musician Yvonne Minton.

programme.title: Horizon
programme.sub-title: The End of the Solar System
programme.desc: This is the story of how our solar system will be transformed by the ageing sun, before coming to a spectacular end in about eight billion years. Astronomers can peer into the far future to predict how it will happen by analysing distant galaxies, stars and even planets in their final moments.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: Twelve billion miles away a spaceship is leaving our solar system and entering the void of deep space. Slowly dying within its heart is a plutonium generator that will beat for perhaps another decade before the lights on Voyager finally go out.

programme.title: Romancing the Stone: The Golden Ages of British Sculpture
programme.desc: Alastair Sooke reveals how sculpture communicates our most cherished beliefs and values, the British soul captured in three dimensions. To begin, he looks at medieval sculpture, from Gothic cathedrals to the misericords underneath church stalls. He shows how sculpture casts a new light on medieval Britain, a more sophisticated, fun-loving and maverick place than commonly believed.

programme.title: The Kenneth Williams Story: A Reputations Special
programme.desc: A look at one of Britain's funniest and most complex comic performer. From a childhood dominated by his adoring mother and bullying father to a lonely suicidal end tortured with regrets, it spans an extraordinary life and career using clips from his unforgettable performances on radio, stage, film and TV; interviews with those who knew him best.

programme.title: Comic Roots
programme.desc: Kenneth Williams explores his roots in and around London's St Pancras, where he grew up. Architecture, poetry, art and music were the formative influences on Kenneth Williams: the slum architecture of St Pancras where he grew up; the liquid poetry of his gran's fruity anecdotes; the art of the Marcel wave practised by his hairdresser father; and the musical knees-up of `The Boot'.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: A Storyville documentary that follows a global team of undercover officers as they penetrate the most hidden corners of the internet to stop those who exploit and harm children.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: When Russia invades Ukraine, a quiet schoolteacher picks up his camera and becomes an unlikely dissident. What emerges is a chilling portrait of how propaganda seeps into everyday life and how even children are drawn into the machinery of war.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: At the African and Caribbean Heritage Centre in Wolverhampton, Michael finds out about the impact of Enoch Powell's 1968 speech on immigration. In Kidderminster, he discovers the site of a secret wartime enterprise known as the Drakelow Tunnels.

programme.title: Gareth Edwards' Great Welsh Adventure
programme.desc: Rugby legend Gareth Edwards and wife Maureen drive a steam train through the epic Dyfi Valley before picking up speed to try rally car driving in the first of their new adventures.

programme.title: Brian Cox's Adventures in Space and Time
programme.desc: Brian explores a simple question that is causing a big stir today: what is time? Modern science shows it to be far stranger than we think. He recalls some highlights from his TV series that touch upon different sides of this physics conundrum.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: Bruce Parry spends time with the Akie people of Tanzania, one of the last groups of hunter-gatherers to live on the African savannah. Bruce is forced to face his biggest fear and put his hand into a bees' nest to gather wild honey.

programme.title: Derek Jacobi Remembers... Breaking the Code
programme.desc: Sir Derek Jacobi looks back on Breaking the Code, the acclaimed 1997 drama that saw him tackling the role of Alan Turing, the mathematical genius who cracked the Enigma code.

programme.title: Breaking the Code
programme.desc: Biography of English mathematician Alan Turing, who was one of the inventors of the digital computer and one of the key figures in the breaking of the Enigma code, used by the Germans to send secret orders to their U-boats in World War II. Turing was also a homosexual in Britain at a time when this was illegal.

programme.title: Castles: Britain's Fortified History
programme.desc: Sam Willis tells the story of the English ruler who left the most indelible mark on the castle - the great Plantagenet king, Edward I who turned it into an instrument of colonisation.

programme.title: Australian F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: A McLaren one-two forms the front row for the Australian Grand Prix, as Lando Norris leads from Oscar Piastri. Max Verstappen starts third, while Lewis Hamilton begins from P8. (16.03)

programme.title: Chinese F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's a first Grand Prix pole for Oscar Piastri as George Russell splits the McLarens with Lando Norris starting third. Sprint winner Lewis Hamilton comes from fifth on the grid. (23.03)

programme.title: Japanese F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out at Suzuka for the Japanese Grand Prix. World champion Max Verstappen starts from the front of the grid with the McLaren duo of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri behind. (06.04)

programme.title: Bahrain F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out for the 2025 Bahrain Grand Prix. Oscar Piastri holds pole position with his McLaren teammate Lando Norris down in P6. Charles Leclerc joins Piastri on the front row. (13.04)

programme.title: Saudi Arabian F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out in Jeddah for the 2025 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix. Reigning world champion Max Verstappen crossed the finish line in P1 last season at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit. (20.04)

programme.title: Miami F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: Polesitter Max Verstappen is joined by Lando Norris and Kimi Antonelli heading into turn one, while Lewis Hamilton tries to fight through the field from P12. (04.05)

programme.title: Emilia Romagna F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out at Imola for the 2025 Emilia Romagna Grand Prix. Last season, reigning world champion Max Verstappen held off a late Lando Norris charge to claim race victory. (18.05)

programme.title: Monaco F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: On the streets of Monte Carlo, the 2025 Monaco Grand Prix arrives. Lando Norris lines up in P1 with Charles Leclerc behind him as the Monegasque pursues back-to-back home wins. (25.05)

programme.title: Spanish F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's an all-papaya front row as McLaren lead the way with Oscar Piastri from Lando Norris. Max Verstappen and George Russell form the second row, while Lewis Hamilton starts P5. (01.06)

programme.title: Canadian F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out for the Canadian Grand Prix as George Russell and Max Verstappen line-up alongside each other at the front with Oscar Piastri in third. Lando Norris comes from P7. (15.06)

programme.title: Austrian F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: Lando Norris bounces back to take pole alongside Charles Leclerc. Oscar Piastri and Lewis Hamilton share row two, while Max Verstappen starts down in P7 for Red Bull's home race. (29.06)

programme.title: British F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out at Silverstone. Max Verstappen shares the front row with Oscar Piastri, while Brits Lando Norris, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton round out the top five. (06.07)

programme.title: Belgian F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out at Spa. With eyes on the weather, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri lock out the front, while Charles Leclerc starts P3. Lewis Hamilton bids to fight through the field. (27.07)

programme.title: Hungarian F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out at the Hungaroring. As Charles Leclerc goes up against the McLarens from pole, both Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton face tough recovery drives from further back. (03.08)

programme.title: Dutch F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out in Zandvoort. Pipping his team mate to pole, Oscar Piastri leads Lando Norris as Max Verstappen looks to spring a surprise from P3 with Isack Hadjar for company. (31.08)

programme.title: Italian F1 GP Highlights
programme.desc: It's lights out at Monza. Max Verstappen holds pole from title contenders Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri as Charles Leclerc leads the Ferrari charge with Lewis Hamilton down in P10. (07.09)
